title: Notification System
summary: Fan out immediate, scheduled and bulk push, SMS and email through queued workers with preferences, delivery tracking and controlled retries.
narrative:
A single user action can spray thousands of notifications: a creator posts and every follower needs a push, SMS or email. The Client here represents product services calling the notification API; scheduled sends and bulk campaigns are additional sources. Keep all channels behind Notification Service, which talks to APNs/FCM for mobile push and to SMS and email providers. Store user contact info, device tokens, preferences, opt-outs and templates in SQL; validate recipient eligibility and select channels before enqueuing, with a final preference/opt-out check at dispatch for delayed sends.

Expect ~10 M notifications/day steady, or ~115/s, plus campaigns of 50 M recipients that must go out within one hour: ~14 K/s, roughly 100× steady traffic. The web tier validates requests, reads SQL and enqueues work, then returns without waiting for delivery. For send-later or bulk campaigns it registers work with Task Scheduler, which fans recipient batches into Message Queue. The queue absorbs bursts while Workers scale independently; provision sustained provider capacity for the one-hour campaign goal because buffering alone cannot meet that deadline.

Wire Client → API Gateway → redundant Web Servers, each connected to Message Queue, SQL and Task Scheduler; the scheduler also enqueues into the queue. Run redundant Workers to drain jobs into Notification Service. Track attempts and status in a NoSQL delivery log keyed by an idempotency key; claim work conditionally and reuse that key at providers that support idempotency. Retries must not double-send: if a provider does not support deduplication, reconcile uncertain outcomes before retrying rather than claiming exactly-once delivery across a network timeout. Retry transient failures with exponential backoff and jitter, then park exhausted jobs in a Dead Letter Queue for inspection and controlled replay. Distinguish provider acceptance from confirmed delivery via available receipts and keep status queryable. Optionally connect Workers to Rate Limiter for per-provider quotas and add Monitoring for queue age, delivery success and DLQ growth.

functional: Accept immediate notification requests from product services and return before delivery
Store user contact info, device tokens, preferences, opt-outs and templates in SQL; resolve channels and recheck delayed-send eligibility at dispatch
Register send-later and bulk campaigns with Task Scheduler; enqueue recipient batches into Message Queue
Have Workers dispatch APNs/FCM push, SMS and email through Notification Service
Use a NoSQL delivery log keyed by idempotency key for conditional work claims, attempts and queryable status; preserve provider deduplication keys across retries
Retry transient failures with exponential backoff and jitter, then park exhausted jobs in a Dead Letter Queue
nonFunctional: A slow or failing provider must not block the triggering request; buffer bulk work and scale Workers independently
A single Worker crash must not stall the pipeline
Support ~10 M notifications/day steady and a 50 M recipient campaign within one hour when provider capacity permits
Distinguish accepted from delivered status; use delivery receipts when available and reconcile ambiguous provider outcomes before retries
constraints: Requests enter through the API Gateway; never send notifications synchronously from the web request path
Connect Task Scheduler to Message Queue for send-later and bulk batches
Keep delivery-log point lookups and conditional writes in NoSQL
Prevent retry double-sends with stable idempotency keys and provider deduplication or uncertain-outcome reconciliation; a delivery log alone cannot guarantee exactly-once external delivery
capacity: 50 M campaign recipients / 3,600 s ≈ 14 K/s within one hour
Bulk throughput is roughly 100× steady traffic; fan out recipient batches through the queue and provision matching provider capacity
specs.tradeoff: A queue-and-worker pipeline trades immediate inline delivery for eventual delivery, independent scaling and recoverable retries. Batching bounds campaign fan-out work, while idempotency and delivery receipts improve reliability; an ambiguous provider timeout still needs provider deduplication or reconciliation before a safe resend.
specs.bonus: Add Monitoring for queue depth, oldest-job age, delivery success and DLQ growth; connect Workers to Rate Limiter to respect per-provider quotas.

topologyRules.message: Don't call the delivery service from the request path — enqueue the work so the request returns fast.
Notifications must flow through the Message Queue and Workers, never straight from the web tier.

resilienceRules.message: Run at least two Workers so one crash doesn't stall the whole delivery pipeline.
A Message Queue needs a Dead Letter Queue so messages that fail after retries are parked, not dropped.
Connect Task Scheduler to Message Queue so scheduled campaigns enter the delivery pipeline.

hints: The web tier validates requests, loads contacts, tokens, preferences and templates from SQL, enqueues work and returns. Start with Client → API Gateway → Web Server → Message Queue and Web Server → SQL.

Wire Message Queue → Worker → Notification Service for APNs/FCM, SMS and email, and Worker → NoSQL for idempotent delivery status. Connect Web Server → Task Scheduler → Message Queue for send-later and bulk batches; retry transient failures with backoff before Message Queue → Dead Letter Queue.

Use two Web Servers, each connected to SQL, Message Queue and Task Scheduler, and two Workers fed by the queue. Each Worker reaches Notification Service and NoSQL; the scheduler enqueues recipient batches and the queue reaches the DLQ. Add each Web Server → Monitoring and each Worker → Rate Limiter for provider quotas.
tips: How to capture notifications - what are the sources?
Where to store them temporarily while they are being processed - Queue? Kafka?
How to deliver the notifications to channels - Mobile push? Email?
Scalability - how does it scale, specially if there is a bulk notification request?
How do you ensure that a notification is delivered?
